title: S cannot close the modal settings panel while a pipe is selected, despite the panel advertising 'S / tap chip to close'
detail: The B1 rework collects S only when sel_pipe < 0, and phase2_blocked now swallows S while the panel is open. Open the panel with a pipe selected and S does nothing — the modal's own advertised close key is dead in a common state.
recommended_fix: Collect S unconditionally while inp.panel_open (the modal gate already makes the lane-key path unreachable via phase2_blocked), keeping the sel_pipe gate only for the closed case.

title: HUD text font sizes scale with ui_scale but the fixed y-positions do not — stacked lines overlap at ×1.25/×1.50
evidence:
+	draw_text(app, "Packet Plumber - v2", 12, 10, rnd.hud(&app.view, 22), p.ink)
+		draw_text(app, "click to place; ESC / right-click cancels", 12, 36, rnd.hud(&app.view, 14), p.ink)
+			draw_text(app, "SURGE SURVIVED - YOU WIN", 12, 68, rnd.hud(&app.view, 30), rl.Color{44, 134, 66, 255})
+		draw_text(app, "press R or Enter to retry (fresh run, fresh seed)", 12, 104, rnd.hud(&app.view, 16), p.ink_soft)
detail: At ×1.50 the title (y=10, size 33) extends to y=43 but the hint still draws at y=36; the win text (y=68, size 45) extends to y=113 but the retry hint still draws at y=104. Font sizes scaled, line anchors not — the lines collide at the knob's own settings.
recommended_fix: Route the y anchors of stacked HUD text lines through hud() (or derive each line from the previous line's scaled height) so spacing scales with the font.

title: QoS manual-editor lane labels and weight values left unscaled while the nudge rects they sit between are scaled — B5 fixed slot 1, missed these
evidence:
for lane in 0..<3 {
			x := QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + lane * 96
			y := qos_row_y(&app.view, 6 + i32(len(app.cat.packet_types)))
			draw_text(app, short[lane], i32(x), y + rnd.hud(&app.view, 4), rnd.hud(&app.view, 14), cols[lane])
			m := qos_nudge_rect(app, i32(lane), true)
			ppp := qos_nudge_rect(app, i32(lane), false)
...
			wv := fmt.tprintf("%d", cur[lane])
			draw_text(app, wv, i32(x + 44), y + 4, 14, p.ink)
---
	x := rnd.hud(&app.view, QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + lane * 96)
detail: qos_nudge_rect scales x through hud() but the 'E/S/B' label and the weight value draw at the raw QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + lane*96, with unscaled y+4 and size 14. At ×1.50 the labels/values no longer align with their −/+ buttons.
recommended_fix: Compute the label/value x with rnd.hud(&app.view, QOS_PANEL_X + 8 + lane * 96) and scale the offsets and text size, matching qos_nudge_rect.

title: effect_settings_adjust claims 'every change lands in the settings file' but the audio row is never persisted
detail: A11y_Settings has no muted field and the file format stores only three payload bytes, so the audio row's settings_save writes unchanged bytes. The panel surfaces AUDIO as a setting; its state silently reverts on relaunch, contradicting the persist claim.
recommended_fix: Either add a muted byte to the settings format (bump SETTINGS_VERSION) or fix the comment to state the audio row is session-only, matching settings.odin's prior-canon note.

title: view.odin claims pulse_read is 'the ONE seam every animated pulse consumer routes through' — the crisis outline consumer bypasses it
detail: draw_crisis_outlines hand-rolls the reduced-motion gate instead of routing through pulse_read. Behavior matches today, but the stated single-seam invariant is false — the next pulse consumer has two patterns to copy.
recommended_fix: Either route the crisis outline through pulse_read or soften the comment to describe pulse_read as the seam for pulse_factor callers only.

title: Forecast + health card backdrops clip off the top window edge at ×1.25/×1.50 (y fixed at 10 while pad scales)
evidence:
card_w := hud(v, 230)
	pad := hud(v, 10)
...
	x := v.win_w - card_w - pad
	y := i32(10)
...
		draw_panel_card(v, x - pad, y - pad, card_w + 2 * pad, h)
---
	card_w := hud(v, 440)
	pad := hud(v, 10)
	x := (v.win_w - card_w) / 2
	y := i32(10)
...
+	rl.DrawRectangle(x - pad, y - pad, card_w + 2 * pad, hud(v, HEALTH_CARD_H), rl.Color{255, 244, 236, 240})
detail: y stays 10 but pad becomes 13/15 at ×1.25/×1.50, so y - pad is −3/−5: the card backdrop + border render partially above the window. Cosmetic, but the B4 rework was specifically about chrome legibility at the knob's max.
recommended_fix: Set y := hud(v, 10) in both procs so the card and its pad scale together.

title: hud_zero_scale test re-implements view_compute's guard inline instead of exercising it — a regression in the real guard cannot fail this test
detail: The B6 coverage test copies the guard into the test body ('emulate view_compute's guard'). Delete the guard from view_compute and this test still passes — it pins its own re-implementation, not the shipped code.
recommended_fix: Call view_compute (or extract the guard into a small helper both call) so the test fails when the real defaulting logic regresses.

title: input.odin comment references SETTINGS_ROWS — the actual constant is SETTINGS_ROW_COUNT
evidence:
panel_open: bool,
	panel_row:  i32, // the focused settings row (0..SETTINGS_ROWS-1)
---
SETTINGS_ROW_COUNT :: 4
detail: The comment names a symbol that does not exist anywhere in the diff; the executor itself uses rnd.SETTINGS_ROW_COUNT. Minor, but it is exactly the kind of stale reference that misleads the next reader.

title: popover_rect scales width via hud_f but passes the height through raw — 'the popover scales with the UI knob' only in one axis
detail: w is scaled, h (POPOVER_H_NODE/PIPE, caller-supplied) is not, and the popover title text still draws at unscaled size 15/offsets. At ×1.50 the demolish button insets scale inside an unscaled-height panel — a wider, same-height popover with mismatched chrome.
recommended_fix: Scale h and the title text/offsets through hud_f as well, or narrow the comment to state only the width and button insets scale.

title: parse_mode_table sets roofs_set before validating elements — a partially malformed roofs array applies zero-value colors, contradicting 'a malformed table leaves that token unset'
detail: If the roofs array has 4 entries but one element is not a json array, roofs_set is already true and that slot stays {0,0,0,0}; palette_apply_mode then installs a transparent-black roof. The tolerant-parse comment promises the base value survives.
recommended_fix: Set roofs_set only after all four elements parse (track a per-element ok flag), or fill failed slots with the default instead of leaving zero values.
